title: Buc-ee's holding mass hiring event for Benton location - NewsBreak
text:
By Blake DeJarnatt ,
5 hours ago
LITTLE ROCK, Ark.- In preparation for the highly anticipated grand opening of Buc-ee’s first Arkansas location, the beaver-branded gas station’s team is hosting a mass hiring event.
Tim Earley, the New Store Opening Manager for Buc-ee’s, says thousands of people have applied to join the crew.
“We received about 6,000 applicants, and out of that we scheduled 1,600 interviews, and we’re going to hire right about 300 plus employees,” Earley said.
Jobs that applicants applied for include Cashier, Janitorial/Cleaning Attendant, Grocery Associate, Food/Deli Associate, and Gift Associate.
Hosted at the Embassy Suites conference room off Financial Parkway in Little Rock, each applicant we spoke with had different reasons why they wanted to join the Buc-ee’s team.
“What sparked my interest was, for one, the healthcare benefits they have, and if you’re working overnights, you get paid like $2 more. Also, they give you three weeks paid time off, you can either use it, let it roll over, or you can cash out on it. That’s good benefits,” said applicant Kardell Allison.
“The pay, and then also when I go to Buc-ee’s, I love the beaver nuggets and the pecans. When I saw it, I was like okay, yeah, why not?,” said Asia Simmons.
Earley said there are a few things that the team is looking for in the interview process that help applicants stand out from the pack.
“Just that they’re bringing effort into the job and that they’re excited to go work for Buc-ee’s. Those individuals that are career minded. They’re not having to have any experience, but we are looking for those individuals that are definitely career minded growing with our company,” Earley said.
Some interviewees, like Simmons and Alisson, were hired on the spot.
“I got a job at Buc-ee’s, I’ll be cleaning y’all’s bathrooms, making sure you have a nice, wonderful experience,” said Simmons.
“I feel pretty encouraged, Buc-ee’s has a lot of better opportunities, has a lot of doors they can open up to you. I’m looking forward to it, I’m looking forward to putting on a Buc-ee’s shirt,” Alisson said.
The mass hiring event began on Tuesday and will conclude Thursday at 4 pm. They were initially accepting walk-in interviews, but after reaching capacity on that front, Earley says Thursday’s interview sessions will be conducted with those who were invited only. However, Earley said people are still encouraged to apply through the Buc-ee’s website for when jobs become available.
Those who received a job offer will now undergo orientation and training in preparation for Buc-ee’s grand opening on Aug. 17.
